Applied.Outcome: Resolved with no reply: all ten recommendations taken. Written into the plan under "Decided before the build".

Replies.Text:
Design, Step 3: One View. Ten decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. The views. State.View keeps read, edit and revisions: the tabs remember them, the links and the hotkeys know them. In CodeMirror mode read and edit are the one editor: document-editor shows edit-view for both and the html-view section in Monaco mode only; a tab left in Read stays Read in its memory, so a switch back to Monaco finds it there. Alternative: normalize read to edit in CodeMirror mode; then every tab would remember Edit. The checks that read "State.View === 'edit'" (Save, the hotkeys) become "the editor is shown".

2. The heading. In Monaco mode the group is Read, Edit, Revisions as today. In CodeMirror mode it is Source (a toggle, id view-source, pressed when on) and Revisions, and Save (id save-button, disabled when clean) with Discard (shown while dirty) move from the edit bar into the heading's first row, right of the group. The edit bar goes in CodeMirror mode; the Stale banner stays, a line above the editor; the "Editing revision N" line goes, the revision being in the heading already. Monaco mode keeps its edit bar.

3. Read-only. An archived plan opens in the editor with editing off (EditorView.editable false and readOnly, a Mirror option), no Save, Source still toggling. The Revisions view in CodeMirror mode shows the revision's text in a second, read-only Live Preview editor in place of its html-view; Monaco mode keeps the html-view. A document opens in the same editor, without marks or buttons but Copy.

4. The live revision. On plan-loaded with a newer revision: clean, the editor takes the new text as one change that leaves the common prefix and suffix alone and replaces the middle, so the cursor and the scroll stay where the text did not move, and the anchors are set afresh from the server's positions; no toast, the revision in the heading changes. Dirty, the Stale banner as today, with Discard. Discard puts the saved text back into the editor and stays there (there is no Read to go to); the draft is forgotten.

5. The dirty dot. The tab-bar shows a dot (class dirty, before the ×, tooltip "unsaved changes") on a tab holding a Draft. The draft is written on every change, the 150 ms delay staying for the Monaco preview alone, so the dot, the memory and Step 4's prompts never lag behind the text.

6. The hotkeys. Ctrl+E in CodeMirror mode toggles Source (the row reads "Source on or off; in Monaco mode Edit, and from Edit save and read"); Ctrl+S saves whenever the editor is shown and dirty; Ctrl+Shift+C when a plan is open. The popup's rows stay twelve.

7. The Editor setting changed while an item is open takes effect at once: the open item re-opens the way the new mode shows it, a draft staying in its tab. Today it waits for the next open.

8. Styles. The heading's new buttons in editor-header.css; the edit bar's rules kept for Monaco mode.

9. Tests. Browser, CodeMirror mode: a plan opens in the editor with Source and Revisions and no Read or Edit; the Source toggle by button and by Ctrl+E; Save from the heading; the dirty dot comes and goes; a newer revision put through the API while clean replaces the text and keeps the cursor; dirty and a newer revision shows Stale; an archived plan is read-only; Revisions shows a read-only editor; the Monaco tests unchanged (they set the editor first). The smoke: the one view.

10. Out of this step: the close prompts (Step 4), the guide (Step 5).

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported; no text change. Committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 3".

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 3: One View. Built as decided, with the notes below; in CodeMirror mode a plan or document opens in the editor, Read and Edit have given way to Source and Revisions, Save and Discard sit in the heading, and Monaco mode is as it was. Resolve to have it committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 3"; reply where something should be otherwise.

What was done

1. The views (decision 1): State.View keeps read, edit and revisions. State gained MirrorShown() (CodeMirror mode with the view Read or Edit: the one editor) and EditorShown() (that, or Monaco's Edit view); document-editor shows edit-view for EditorShown and the Read section only when the CodeMirror editor is not the view; every check that read "the view is edit" (Save, the Save hotkey, the pending, the compose and the re-anchor staying put, New Comment, Ctrl+Shift+C) reads one of the two now. A tab left in Read stays Read in its memory.
2. The heading (2): in Monaco mode Read, Edit, Revisions as before; in CodeMirror mode Source (id view-source, pressed when on; from Revisions it also brings the editor back) and Revisions (pressed again, the editor comes back), then Save (id save-button, disabled while clean, stale, busy or archived) and Discard (shown while dirty or stale). The heading reaches the editor through State.Editing, which edit-view sets to its controller. In CodeMirror mode the edit bar is gone; a stale edit is said in a line above the editor, naming the revision that arrived.
3. Read-only (3): Mirror takes Options.ReadOnly and SetReadOnly( On ) (a compartment with EditorState.readOnly and EditorView.editable); an archived plan opens read-only, and is re-opened when its archived state changes under it; the Revisions view in CodeMirror mode shows the revision's text in a second read-only Live Preview editor in place of its html-view, made once the element is in the page and let go when the setting goes back to Monaco; a document opens in the same editor, without marks, with Copy alone (Step 2).
4. The live revision (4): on plan-loaded with the same plan at a newer revision, a clean text takes the new one as a single change over the middle that differs (the common prefix and suffix left alone), so the cursor and the scroll stay, the base moves on, the draft is forgotten and the anchors are set from the server's positions, with no toast; a dirty text shows the stale line with Discard, which puts the saved text back into the editor and stays there. Monaco takes a clean newer text whole. A load that brings another plan, or a change of the archived state, re-opens the editor.
5. The dirty dot (5): the tab-bar shows a dot before the tab's buttons while the tab holds a draft (class dirty on the tab, tooltip "unsaved changes"); the draft is written on every change now, the 150 ms delay kept for the Monaco preview alone.
6. The hotkeys (6): Ctrl+E in CodeMirror mode toggles Source and, from Revisions, brings the editor back; in Monaco mode as before; the row reads "Source on or off; in Monaco mode Edit, and from Edit save and read". Ctrl+S saves whenever the editor is shown. The rows stay twelve.
7. The Editor setting (7) takes effect at once: edit-view re-opens on editor-changed when it is shown, letting the other engine go, the draft coming back from the tab; the revisions view drops its reader on the way back to Monaco.
8. Styles (8): the stale line in edit-view.css, the dot in tab-bar.css, the reader's box in revisions-view.css; the edit bar's rules kept for Monaco mode; the heading's buttons needed no rule of their own.
9. Tests (9): the three CodeMirror browser tests no longer press Edit (the editor is the view) and read view-source; a new test drives the one view: the editor at once with Source, Revisions and Save in the heading and no Read, Edit or edit bar; Source by the button and back by Ctrl+E; an edit lighting Save and dotting the tab, Save from the heading making the revision and clearing both; a newer revision from the API while clean taken silently with the cursor still at the end; a newer revision while dirty showing the stale line with Save off, Discard bringing the server's text back; Revisions as a read-only editor and the editor back on the second press; an archived plan read-only and editable again once restored; back to Monaco with Read and Edit and the Read view. node --test: 195 pass (194 before: one browser test added), the whole suite run to the end once the drags retried. The smoke no longer presses Edit in CodeMirror mode and checks the one view; the whole smoke (page and desktop) ends SMOKE OK with 41 checks.

Notes and departures

- Revisions is a toggle too: pressed while shown, the editor comes back. The design named only Source for the way back; both do it now, since a pressed button that does nothing on a second press reads wrong.
- The heading reads the editor's Dirty, Stale and Busy and calls its Save and Discard through State.Editing, the edit-view's controller set on State; a service of its own for five members seemed more than the thing warranted.
- A second open while the engine is still being created waits for it, so a plan-loaded arriving during the first open does not make two editors; the view-changed to Read that OpenPlan sends before the new plan is loaded still opens the editor on the old plan for a moment, which costs nothing visible.
- The smoke ran twice: the first run, beside the whole test suite, stopped at the connect screen's overlay check (a height compared within a pixel while the machine was loaded); alone it ended SMOKE OK. The threads-in-the-editor test of Step 2 missed its drag once under the whole suite as well; its drags are tried up to three times now, and the line is given 300 ms to settle after the scroll.
- The server tests ran untouched.
